note: Every UPSC CSE Prelims and Mains question format, and the templates that practise it. Format descriptions follow the public exam pattern; they are not previous-year questions. Optional-subject papers are out of scope. The interview (personality test) has one format so far, covered by hidden-why.

papers.prelims-gs1: Prelims GS Paper I (100 MCQs, 2 marks each, one-third negative marking)
papers.prelims-csat: Prelims CSAT, GS Paper II (qualifying, 33%; 80 MCQs)
papers.mains-gs1: Mains GS1: Indian heritage and culture, history, geography of the world and society
papers.mains-gs2: Mains GS2: governance, Constitution, polity, social justice, international relations
papers.mains-gs3: Mains GS3: technology, economy, environment, biodiversity, security, disaster management
papers.mains-gs4: Mains GS4: ethics, integrity and aptitude
papers.mains-qualifying: Mains qualifying papers: Paper A (an Indian language) and Paper B (English)

formats.name: Direct MCQ
formats.desc: One question, four options, one right answer: a fact, a concept or an application.

formats.name: Negative stem
formats.desc: "Which one of the following is NOT ..." or "is incorrect". The trap is reading it as a positive question.

formats.name: Statements with codes
formats.desc: Two to four numbered statements, then "Which of the statements given above is/are correct?" with codes such as 1 only, 2 only, both, neither.

formats.name: Select the items (codes)
formats.desc: A numbered list of items, then "Select the correct answer using the code given below" (1 and 2 only, 1, 2 and 3 ...).

formats.name: How many statements are correct
formats.desc: Only one, only two, all three or none. Codes no longer help elimination, so every statement must be judged.

formats.name: How many pairs are correctly matched
formats.desc: Three or four pairs (place and state, term and meaning), and the member counts the correct ones.

formats.name: Statement I and Statement II
formats.desc: Two statements; decide whether each is true and whether II explains I. The older assertion-and-reason format.

formats.name: Statement I, II and III
formats.desc: Do Statements II and III both hold, and does each explain Statement I?

formats.name: Match List I with List II
formats.desc: Two lists matched with codes, or pairs matched directly.

formats.name: Arrange in order
formats.desc: Chronological order, north to south, largest to smallest, upstream to downstream.

formats.name: Location and map
formats.desc: Where a place, river, park or strait is, what it borders, which lies furthest east, and so on.

formats.name: Current affairs on a static base
formats.desc: A recent event used to test the concept behind it.

formats.name: Numbers, reports and indices
formats.desc: Who publishes which index, what it measures, and order-of-magnitude facts.

formats.name: Reading comprehension
formats.desc: A passage, then the main idea, an inference, the assumption behind it, or the most logical corollary.

formats.name: Basic numeracy
formats.desc: Percentages, ratios, averages, time and work, speed and distance, number properties.

formats.name: Logical and analytical reasoning
formats.desc: Syllogisms, direction sense, blood relations, arrangements, coding and series.

formats.name: Data interpretation
formats.desc: A table or chart, then questions that need a calculation from it.

formats.name: Directive-word answer (10 and 15 marks)
formats.desc: 150 or 250 words to discuss, critically examine, analyse, elucidate, comment and so on, with an introduction, a body and a conclusion.

formats.name: Reading the directive word
formats.desc: What "discuss", "critically examine" or "to what extent" asks for, and the mistake each invites.

formats.name: Diagram, flowchart or map in an answer
formats.desc: A quick sketch that carries the answer: a process flow, a cycle, a labelled map.

formats.name: Both sides and way forward
formats.desc: Arguments for and against, then a balanced conclusion and a way forward.

formats.name: Ethics concepts and thinkers
formats.desc: Define and distinguish terms (integrity, probity, empathy), and the contributions of thinkers.

formats.name: What does this quote mean to you?
formats.desc: A quotation by a thinker, to be explained in the present context with an example.

formats.name: Case study
formats.desc: A scenario with stakeholders, ethical issues, options with merits and demerits, and a course of action.

formats.name: Essay (philosophical or issue-based)
formats.desc: 1,000 to 1,200 words on a quote-like or issue theme, read across many dimensions, with a strong opening and close.

formats.name: Qualifying essay
formats.desc: A shorter essay in the chosen Indian language (Paper A) or English (Paper B).

formats.name: Précis
formats.desc: Reduce a passage to about one-third of its length, with a title, in your own words.

formats.name: Comprehension
formats.desc: A passage with questions answered in your own words.

formats.name: Translation
formats.desc: English to the Indian language and back, in Paper A.

formats.name: Grammar and usage
formats.desc: Correct the sentence, use a word or idiom, give a synonym or antonym.

formats.name: Talking about ideas in the interview
formats.desc: Explaining a concept or a piece of evidence clearly and honestly when the board asks for your view, including what the evidence does not show.
